note: Sizes that set how an organelle is drawn on the Machines view's shelf and rest on a paper whose licence is non-commercial: held here, in the project's files, and never carried by the page. tools/build_catalogue.py reads this file and writes into a bench only the size drawn and the words for its basis; the scene, the benches, the catalogue's core and every file the export publishes carry none of these numbers and no name of these papers (tests/licence_classes.test.mjs). The contract is schema/MACHINE_CATALOGUE.md, "Organelles".
decided: On 20 November 2026 the owner ruled that numbers from papers under non-commercial licences may be cited in the project's files and may set how a thing is drawn, and are not shown in the page.

nucleus.page_words: near the size of a HeLa nucleus inside the cell

read.results: “The nuclear volume increased 2.47 times from G1 (510 ± 121 μm3) to late S-G2 phase (1263 ± 129 μm3)”
read.figure: The legend of Fig. 3E: “means ± SE”; mean volumes 658 μm3 (asynchronous, n = 32 cells), 510 μm3 (G1, n = 36 cells), 1263 μm3 (late S-G2, n = 37 cells)
read.method: Formaldehyde-fixed HeLa cells, DAPI-stained nuclei, confocal image stacks, surfaces by Imaris (its Methods, “Nuclear volume measurement”)

nucleus.working: Ours, not the paper's: a sphere of 510 μm3 is 9.9 µm across and one of 658 μm3 is 10.8 µm; drawn 10 µm.

source.text: Iida S and others (2022) Science Advances 8:eabn5626. Read by the visualizer coordinator as Europe PMC full text PMC9166292 on 20 November 2026.
source.licence: “Creative Commons Attribution NonCommercial License 4.0”, as the article states

centriole.page_words: near the size of a centriole in the bone marrow cells of healthy people

read.results: Section 2.2, on CD138-negative bone marrow mononuclear cells of three healthy donors: “the median length of centrioles (368 nm, range: 190–753 nm) was normal in these cells” and “their median diameter (204 nm, range: 182–226 nm) was slightly reduced”, of 205 completely pictured centrioles
read.method: A screen by transmission electron microscopy, then serial electron tomography of each centriole found (its Results and STAR Methods)

centriole.working: Ours, not the paper's: the two medians rounded to one figure each, drawn about 0.2 µm across and 0.4 µm long (decided on 20 November 2026: a held number is not shown in the page, and the length's median to two figures would have been).

source.text: Dittrich and others (2022) A high-throughput electron tomography workflow reveals over-elongated centrioles in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma. Cell Reports Methods 2(11):100322. Read as Europe PMC full text PMC9701608 on 20 November 2026.
source.licence: “an open access article under the CC BY-NC-ND license”, as the article states

endocytic-vesicle.page_words: near the size of the small vesicles and tubules that carry Rab5 in HeLa cells

read.results: Results, “CLEM of Rab5 and Rab7 reveals differential distributions over early to late endolysosomal compartments”: “The Rab5-positive vesicle-tubules were 100–200 nm in diameter and often found near the plasma membrane.” Methods, “Definition of endolysosomes by EM morphology”: early endosomes are defined “as irregularly shaped electron-lucent vacuoles containing fewer than six ILVs”, with no size
read.method: HeLa cells; correlative light and electron microscopy on sections (immunofluorescence on cryosections, then transmission electron microscopy of the same sections)

endocytic-vesicle.working: Ours, not the paper's: drawn at the middle of the range, 0.15 µm across. The paper gives no size of an early endosome, so what it measured stands on the shelf as an endocytic vesicle, not as an early endosome.

source.text: van der Beek and others (2021) Quantitative correlative microscopy reveals the ultrastructural distribution of endogenous endosomal proteins. Journal of Cell Biology 221(1):e202106044. Read as Europe PMC full text PMC8624803 on 20 November 2026.
source.licence: “Attribution–Noncommercial–Share Alike 4.0 International license”, after six months under a licence with no mirror sites, as the article states
